today_summary: GCM26 marks $4,376 with ATM IV 21.56% and a heavily call-skewed chain — 224,187 call OI against 86,066 put OI (P/C 0.38). The $4,500 call wall is the dominant structure at 12,419 contracts, just $124 (2.1σ) overhead, while the nearest meaningful put support sits back at $4,300 (3,457). Cumulative net GEX is negative from $2,925 all the way up to the $4,700 flip, leaving spot $324 inside short-gamma territory even though the local ±$200 slab reads +168 on the strength of that one call wall. Max pain $5,500 is $1,124 above spot and carries no pull at 63 DTE — ignore it as a magnet.
five_day_thesis: Five sessions produced almost no net price movement (-$10.80, $4,387 → $4,376) but a clear one-way shift in positioning. ATM IV compressed 24.10% → 21.56% (-2.54pp, -10.5% relative) and has now been pinned flat for two sessions, while total options volume collapsed 47% from the 9/18 peak (14,211 → 7,531 contracts) — participation is draining, not rotating. The $4,500 call wall thickened through the decline, +290 contracts to 12,419, meaning sellers added supply into weakness rather than covering; $4,000 puts simultaneously grew +147 to 4,043 as downside hedges went on. The gamma flip has not moved off $4,700 on four of five sessions (a lone $4,680 print on 9/21), so spot has spent the entire week trapped below it in an amplifying regime with no attempt at reclaim. Max pain drifted down $5,570 → $5,500 and P/C OI never budged from 0.38, confirming this is the same structure decaying in place, not a repositioning.
